Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the quick intro call last week. As discussed, we're collecting firm-level answers from vendors for an identity and access controls RFP. I've attached our SCIM spec and a short spreadsheet — the core items we need from Redwood:

- SAML & OIDC support: IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows, assertion attributes, algorithm support, and logout semantics.
- SCIM behavior: bulk sync (initial/full), incremental delta support, attribute filtering, group handling, and delete/deprovision semantics.
- RBAC and admin controls: admin roles, delegated admin, session controls, MFA enforcement for admin actions.
- Multi-tenant scoping: can we guarantee tenant-level isolation of directory syncs and admin scope?
- Audit & evidence: where are admin events audited, retention windows, and examples of exportable audit logs.

Could you please send a filled capability response and any artifacts (attribute-map CSV, short diagrams) by end of day Tuesday PST? We may follow with a short technical Q&A.

Subject: Re: Questionnaire: SAML/OIDC, SCIM, RBAC — multi-tenant scoping (Acropolis Capital)

Elena — thanks for the note and the spec. We can absolutely provide these details. I'm attaching our capability packet and a SCIM attribute-mapping CSV that matches the fields in your doc. High-level responses below; full answers are in the attached PDF: Redwood_IAM_Capabilities_20270605.pdf and scim-attribute-mapping.csv.

- SAML/OIDC: We support SP- and IdP-initiated SAML 2.0; OIDC provider and RP flows with id_token and access_token claims; SHA-256 signatures; optional ACR claims for step-up. Logout: SLO via back-channel and front-channel supported for SAML; OIDC RP-initiated logout supported.
- SCIM: SCIM v2 with support for full sync and incremental changes via listResources with startIndex/totalResults. We provide pagination and delta tokens for incremental sync. Group membership is represented via group objects with members array; we support PATCH bulk operations for efficient updates.
- RBAC/admin: Built-in roles (Account Admin, Org Admin, Billing Admin, Read-Only Auditor) with granular route-level permissions. Delegated admin via scoped admin tokens and admin scoping per-tenant. We support conditional MFA enforcement for admin sessions.
- Multi-tenant scoping: each provisioned tenant receives a unique directory namespace and isolated data stores for KV and KV-cache; admin scopes are tenant-scoped by default. For shared/integrated directories we provide tag-based isolation and explicit consented mapping.
- Auditing: Admin actions are written to immutable audit streams; retention is configurable (default 365 days) and exports are available as newline-delimited JSON.

Proposed next step: a 30-minute technical call early next week to walk the SCIM attribute mapping and deletion semantics. I'm available Mon/Tue 10–12 PST.

Attachments: Redwood_IAM_Capabilities_20270605.pdf (summary + diagrams), scim-attribute-mapping.csv

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Thanks Soojin — the packet looks helpful. A few clarifying questions before we lock in a call:

1) SCIM deletion semantics: does Redwood support hard-delete vs. soft-delete configurable per-tenancy? If soft-delete, is there a tombstone window and a guaranteed eventual purge?
2) Delta tokens & ordering: when using incremental sync, what guarantees do you provide around ordering and idempotence for concurrent updates from multiple identity sources?
3) Group membership size/perf: our largest tenant has ~120k members in a single group; any known limits or recommended sharding approaches?
4) Admin audit exports: can we configure log forwarding to our SIEM (S3/Kinesis/Datadog) and are export schemas documented?

I've attached our SCIM spec to highlight a few attributes (externalId, officeLocation, costCenter map) — please call out exact attribute names in your CSV that you can accept. Also include any differences between SCIM push vs. pull workflows for provisioning.

Best,
Elena
